name: Rye bread (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Rye bread [Cereals and cereal products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 172684 (Bread, rye) - full nutrient panel: macros, sugars, 18 amino acids, minerals, vitamins, fatty acids

Scald fermentation rye bread, Foods/Nutrients 2025, PMC11941048 - sugars (maltose 12-13% dw, glucose/fructose/sucrose) and organic acids (lactic 0.81-2.06, acetic 0.16-0.23, succinic 0.03-0.17 g/100g dw)
LAB starter wholemeal rye bread, PMC8759695 - lactic/acetic acid and fermentation quotient
FODMAP fingerprinting of bakery products & sourdoughs, PMC8074121 - fructose, FOS/fructans, mannitol in rye and rye sourdough
Sourdough organic-acid survey ranges (lactic 0.22-0.87, acetic 0.07-0.10 g/100g fw)
FooDB FOOD00809 (Rye bread) - base record and phenolic/alkylresorcinol coverage
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources are STARCH (~39 g/100g) and its hydrolysis product MALTOSE (~2.5 g/100g, the main residual free sugar after yeast/LAB fermentation); LACTIC ACID (~0.6 g/100g, added here - was missing) is the defining sourdough metabolite and a key organic-acid carbon source, with acetic and succinic acids from heterofermentative LAB. Sugar split is anchored to the measured USDA total sugars (3.8 g/100g) with maltose-dominant proportions from rye-bread HPLC literature; organic acid
curation_added: lactic acid (dominant sourdough organic acid, ~0.6 g/100g) - absent from FooDB record
acetic acid (~0.15 g/100g) - absent from FooDB record
succinic acid (~0.05 g/100g) - absent from FooDB record
maltose apportioned as the dominant free sugar (~2.5 g/100g within USDA total sugars 3.8)
quantitative amounts for all sugars, amino acids, minerals, vitamins, fatty acids from USDA FDC 172684
mannitol (rye-sourdough LAB fermentation product; present but unquantified in baked bread)
explicit starch amount (~38.7 g/100g) as the dominant carbon source
L-serine to replace the D-serine artifact

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
